SEASONALITY — LIFTS (re-checked 30 Aug 2026 against the Chamonix valley 2026 summer schedule): Aiguille du Midi, the Montenvers / Mer de Glace train and Brévent all run to 1 NOVEMBER 2026, then close for maintenance until mid-December. La Flégère closes 13 SEPTEMBER and Le Tour / Balme closes 20 SEPTEMBER. So the three headline lifts are safe for all of October, but the Flégère side of the valley — including the usual lift-assisted approach to Lac Blanc — is already shut. Lac Blanc in October is a full walk-up from Les Praz, roughly 12 km round trip with 1,100 m of climb: doable but hard. The easier October alternatives are Lac Cornu, the Petit Balcon Sud, and the Mer de Glace via the train.

SEASONALITY — PASSES: Col de l'Iseran and Col du Galibier normally stay open into November but are weather-closed from mid-October in bad years (both shut on 20 October in 2025). This itinerary deliberately does NOT route over them — they sit in the Maurienne, east of the route, and are a detour, not a necessity.

FALLBACK ROUTES (all low-altitude, open year-round): Col des Aravis and Col de la Colombière between Chamonix and Annecy; the Route des Gorges / Combe Laval and Grands Goulets balcony roads in the Vercors; and the Pierres Dorées lanes in Beaujolais. If a high pass shuts, nothing in the plan breaks.

ROUTING: Geneva (GVA, 1h to Chamonix) in, Lyon (LYS) out. One-way rental across the Swiss-French border is normal but confirm the drop fee; renting on the French side of GVA avoids the Swiss motorway vignette.

ROUTING: the Luberon was considered and dropped in favour of Beaujolais and Lyon. The Luberon is another 3h south of Grenoble and would break the driving budget on a 14-day trip; Beaujolais gives the same market-and-food finish 1h from the departure airport.
TIMING: if the trip lands in late October rather than early, add a buffer day in Chamonix — the Aiguille du Midi is frequently wind-held, and there is no second chance after 1 November.

CARD CAPTIONS — PRIMARY (migrated 2026-08-30): Chamonix & Mont Blanc: Three nights; the three main lifts run to 1 November 2026. | Annecy & Its Lake: Three nights, with the lake a five-minute walk from the old town. | The Vercors Balcony Roads: Three nights based at Villard-de-Lans.

CARD CAPTIONS — NATURE (migrated 2026-08-30): Mer de Glace: Montenvers railway runs to 1 November 2026. | Lac Blanc: Flégère lift shuts 13 September, so from October it's a 12 km walk-up. | Cirque de Saint-Même: Easy 6 km loop; the car park fills at weekends. | The Vercors Plateau: Low enough to stay clear long after the high Alps have snow. | Lake Annecy Shore Path: Flat and paved for 33 km; bikes rent by the hour in town.

CARD CAPTIONS — CITIES (migrated 2026-08-30): Chamonix: Aiguille du Midi and Brévent both run to 1 November 2026. | Annecy: Markets Tuesday and Sunday mornings in the old town. | Grenoble: The cable car runs year-round, five minutes from the centre. | Oingt & the Pierres Dorées: An hour from Lyon, twenty minutes off the A6. | Vieux Lyon: Traboules are free to walk; the covered food halls are ten minutes away. | Chambéry: A natural lunch stop on the Annecy–Vercors drive.

CARD CAPTIONS — FOOD (migrated 2026-08-30): Tartiflette: Invented in the 1980s by the Reblochon makers — none the worse for it. | Raclette: Priced per person; the melting machine comes to the table. | Annecy Market Day: Tuesday, Friday and Sunday mornings in the old town. | Lyonnais Bouchon Cooking: Daniel et Denise and Café des Fédérations are the long-standing ones. | Savoyard Cheese Shops: Beaufort d'alpage is the summer-milk version, and the one to buy. | Les Halles Paul Bocuse: Closed Mondays; busiest and best on a Sunday morning.

destination: French Alps — Chamonix, Annecy & the Vercors
title: Mont Blanc to the Markets: An Eastern France Road Trip

heroImage.caption: The Mont Blanc massif above the Chamonix valley

brief: The Alps you already love, on the French side. A cable car to 3,842 m under Mont Blanc, a turquoise lake ringed by mountains at Annecy, limestone balcony roads carved into cliffs in the Vercors, and then a soft landing in the food country north of Lyon. Big scenery early, markets and comfort at the end.

facts.bestSeason: Early October — the three main Chamonix lifts run to 1 November, but mid-altitude lifts have already closed
facts.language: French; English is fine in Chamonix and Annecy, thinner in the Vercors
facts.timezone: Central European Time (UTC+2 until 25 October, then UTC+1)
facts.driving: Right-hand traffic, superb roads, one-way rental across the border

primary.heading: Glacier, lake, limestone
primary.intro: The trip climbs high early and comes down slowly — a cable car under Mont Blanc, then a lake town, then cliff roads, then market country north of Lyon.

nature.heading: Ice above, water below
nature.intro: Chamonix has the glaciers and the altitude. Annecy has the clearest lake in Europe. The Vercors has limestone cirques and roads blasted into vertical rock.

cities.heading: Mountain towns that stay awake
cities.intro: These are year-round towns rather than resorts — Chamonix has hardware shops and supermarkets, Annecy has markets twice a week, and Lyon has the covered food halls.

food.heading: Cheese, potatoes, repeat
food.intro: Savoyard cooking is unapologetic: melted cheese over potatoes, cured ham, and village dairies selling Beaufort by the wheel. Then Lyon, which takes all of it very seriously.

why.heading: The Alps with the season working for you
why.intro: Everything that matters is still running in October, and the trip gets warmer and easier the further south it goes.

thingsToDo.heading: Rack railways, caves and a postman's palace
thingsToDo.intro: The Alps do the big scenery on their own. These are the days out that give it some variety — a train to a glacier, a cave with a river in it, and one genuinely mad building.

itinerary.description: Land in the evening, sleep near the airport, and be in the mountains within an hour of waking up.
The cable car to the Aiguille du Midi, the rack railway to the Mer de Glace, and valley-floor walks under the whole Mont Blanc massif.
A canal-laced old town on a startlingly clear lake, the Tuesday and Sunday markets, and an easy lakeside cycle path.
Cliff-cut balcony roads, deep forest, quiet plateau hikes, and Grenoble's cable-car viewpoint 40 minutes away.
Golden-stone villages, proper covered food markets, and the old town of Lyon — the food capital, done casually.
Twenty minutes to the airport from Beaujolais, and home.

primaryHighlights.title: Chamonix & Mont Blanc
primaryHighlights.description: A cable car straight up to 3,842 metres and a glacier train into the Mer de Glace — both running until 1 November.
primaryHighlights.caption: Aiguille du Midi summit station

primaryHighlights.title: Annecy & Its Lake
primaryHighlights.description: Maybe the prettiest small city in France — canals, painted houses, mountain backdrop, and one of the cleanest lakes in Europe.
primaryHighlights.caption: Lake Annecy and the Alps

primaryHighlights.title: The Vercors Balcony Roads
primaryHighlights.description: Roads blasted into vertical limestone cliffs, tunnels with windows cut in the side — driving as the main event.
primaryHighlights.caption: Road tunnel cut into Combe Laval

natureHighlights.title: Mer de Glace
natureHighlights.description: France's largest glacier, reached by a red rack railway from the middle of Chamonix. No hiking required.
natureHighlights.caption: The Mer de Glace valley

natureHighlights.title: Lac Blanc
natureHighlights.description: The classic Mont Blanc reflection — a mountain lake with the whole massif standing in it.
natureHighlights.caption: Turquoise water of Lac Blanc

natureHighlights.title: Cirque de Saint-Même
natureHighlights.description: A horseshoe of cliffs with four waterfalls stacked one above the other, deep in the Chartreuse.
natureHighlights.caption: Limestone cliffs at Saint-Même

natureHighlights.title: The Vercors Plateau
natureHighlights.description: Rolling forest and meadow at 1,000 m, with gentle marked trails running right through it.
natureHighlights.caption: Aerial view of the Vercors massif

natureHighlights.title: Lake Annecy Shore Path
natureHighlights.description: An old railway line along the shore, water on one side and mountains on the other the whole way.
natureHighlights.caption: Boats along the Annecy shoreline

cityHighlights.title: Chamonix
cityHighlights.description: A real mountain town rather than a purpose-built resort — open all year, with shops, supermarkets and gear stores.
cityHighlights.caption: Chamonix's Hôtel de Ville facade

cityHighlights.title: Annecy
cityHighlights.description: Canals, arcades and pastel houses, plus one of the best open-air markets in the Alps twice a week.
cityHighlights.caption: Canal in old town Annecy

cityHighlights.title: Grenoble
cityHighlights.description: A big city ringed by mountains, with a fort on the hill above it and glass bubbles going up.
cityHighlights.caption: Grenoble seen from Mont Jalla

cityHighlights.title: Oingt & the Pierres Dorées
cityHighlights.description: Beaujolais villages built entirely from golden limestone, on lanes made for a nice car.
cityHighlights.caption: Oingt village above the vineyards

cityHighlights.title: Vieux Lyon
cityHighlights.description: Renaissance streets in pale stone, with hidden passageways cut straight through the buildings.
cityHighlights.caption: A narrow street in Vieux Lyon

cityHighlights.title: Chambéry
cityHighlights.description: The old capital of Savoy — arcaded streets, a castle, and a fountain held up by four stone elephants, halfway between Annecy and the Vercors.
cityHighlights.caption: Rooftops of old Chambéry

culinaryHighlights.title: Tartiflette
culinaryHighlights.description: Potatoes, bacon and a whole wheel of Reblochon baked into one dish. Savoie's answer to a cold afternoon.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Tartiflette fresh from the oven

culinaryHighlights.title: Raclette
culinaryHighlights.description: Melted cheese scraped straight onto potatoes and cured meat — the decadent, cheesy, flagship dish of the French alps.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Raclette being scraped tableside

culinaryHighlights.title: Annecy Market Day
culinaryHighlights.description: Trestle tables down every lane of the old town, piled with mountain cheese, charcuterie, bread and produce.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Cheese stalls in old Annecy

culinaryHighlights.title: Lyonnais Bouchon Cooking
culinaryHighlights.description: Small, loud rooms on paper tablecloths doing quenelles, pork and gratins — the quenelle is a pike dumpling the size of your fist.
culinaryHighlights.caption: A quenelle in cream sauce

culinaryHighlights.title: Savoyard Cheese Shops
culinaryHighlights.description: Beaufort, Abondance, Tomme and Reblochon, from village dairies all the way down the valley.
culinaryHighlights.caption: A cheese-ageing cellar

culinaryHighlights.title: Les Halles Paul Bocuse
culinaryHighlights.description: Lyon's covered food market — fifty stalls of charcuterie, cheese, bread and pastry under one roof, with counters to eat at between them.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Inside Les Halles Paul Bocuse

thingsToDo.title: Tramway du Mont-Blanc
thingsToDo.description: France's highest rack railway, grinding up from Saint-Gervais to 2,372 m at the Nid d'Aigle, right under the glaciers.
thingsToDo.caption: The Tramway du Mont-Blanc railcar

thingsToDo.title: Palais Idéal du Facteur Cheval
thingsToDo.description: A rural postman spent 33 years building a fantasy palace out of stones he picked up on his round. It is as strange as that sounds.
thingsToDo.caption: Facade of the Palais Idéal

thingsToDo.title: Grottes de Choranche
thingsToDo.description: A cave under the Vercors cliffs hung with thousands of thin, translucent straw stalactites, with an underground river running through.
thingsToDo.caption: Straw stalactites in Choranche cave

thingsToDo.title: A Beaufort Cheese Cellar
thingsToDo.description: Village dairies age Beaufort in vaulted cellars stacked with 40 kg wheels, and sell it over the counter at the door.
thingsToDo.caption: Wheels of Beaufort on shelves

thingsToDo.title: Lyon's Traboules
thingsToDo.description: Covered passageways cut straight through the blocks of the old town, linking street to street through courtyards and spiral stairs. Most are unmarked and free to walk.
thingsToDo.caption: A vaulted traboule passageway

otherPerks: The Aiguille du Midi runs to 1 November — 3,842 m by cable car, no walking involved
Mer de Glace by rack railway: a glacier at the end of a train ride
Annecy's lake is the cleanest in Europe, with a flat 33 km path around the shore
Beaufort and Reblochon straight from village dairies, at dairy prices
Balcony roads through the Vercors, with tunnels cut open to the drop
Markets twice a week in Annecy and covered food halls in Lyon
Autumn colour in the valleys while the peaks already have fresh snow
Everything is about an hour apart, so no day is spent in the car
